cards.front: What are the steps that bring neutrophils from the blood into inflamed tissue?
cards.back: **Margination** → **rolling** (endothelial **E- and P-selectin** bind sialyl Lewis X) → **firm adhesion** (neutrophil **integrins** bind **ICAM-1**) → **transmigration** through postcapillary venules (PECAM-1) → **chemotaxis** toward C5a, LTB4, IL-8 and bacterial peptides.
cards.back_pt: **Marginação** → **rolamento** (**E-selectina e P-selectina** endoteliais se ligam ao sialil Lewis X) → **adesão firme** (**integrinas** do neutrófilo se ligam à **ICAM-1**) → **transmigração** pelas vênulas pós-capilares (PECAM-1) → **quimiotaxia** em direção a C5a, LTB4, IL-8 e peptídeos bacterianos.

cards.front: How does an inflammatory exudate differ from a transudate?
cards.back: **Exudate**: inflammation makes venules leaky, so the fluid is **rich in protein and cells** (high specific gravity). **Transudate**: vessels stay intact; high hydrostatic or low oncotic pressure pushes out fluid **poor in protein and cells** (e.g., heart failure, nephrotic syndrome).
cards.back_pt: **Exsudato**: a inflamação torna as vênulas permeáveis, e o líquido é **rico em proteínas e células** (densidade alta). **Transudato**: os vasos ficam íntegros; pressão hidrostática alta ou oncótica baixa empurra para fora um líquido **pobre em proteínas e células** (ex.: insuficiência cardíaca, síndrome nefrótica).

cards.front: Which mediators explain each cardinal sign of acute inflammation?
cards.back: **Redness and heat**: arteriolar dilation (histamine, prostaglandins, NO). **Swelling**: leaky venules (histamine, bradykinin, leukotrienes C4/D4/E4). **Pain**: **bradykinin** and **PGE2** sensitize nerve endings. **Loss of function** follows pain and swelling.
cards.back_pt: **Rubor e calor**: dilatação arteriolar (histamina, prostaglandinas, NO). **Tumor (edema)**: vênulas permeáveis (histamina, bradicinina, leucotrienos C4/D4/E4). **Dor**: **bradicinina** e **PGE2** sensibilizam as terminações nervosas. **Perda de função** decorre da dor e do edema.

cards.front: Which cells define chronic inflammation, and what happens in the tissue?
cards.back: **Macrophages** (the central cell), **lymphocytes** and **plasma cells**. Tissue destruction, **angiogenesis** and **fibrosis** go on at the same time. Causes: persistent infection, autoimmune disease, or long exposure to a harmful agent.
cards.back_pt: **Macrófagos** (a célula central), **linfócitos** e **plasmócitos**. Destruição tecidual, **angiogênese** e **fibrose** ocorrem ao mesmo tempo. Causas: infecção persistente, doença autoimune ou exposição prolongada a um agente nocivo.

cards.front: What is a granuloma, and which diseases cause caseating vs noncaseating granulomas?
cards.back: A nodule of **epithelioid macrophages**, often with **multinucleated giant cells**, rimmed by lymphocytes. **Caseating** (central necrosis): **tuberculosis**, fungi (histoplasmosis, coccidioidomycosis). **Noncaseating**: **sarcoidosis**, **Crohn disease**, berylliosis, foreign bodies.
cards.back_pt: Nódulo de **macrófagos epitelioides**, muitas vezes com **células gigantes multinucleadas**, cercado por linfócitos. **Caseoso** (necrose central): **tuberculose**, fungos (histoplasmose, coccidioidomicose). **Não caseoso**: **sarcoidose**, **doença de Crohn**, beriliose, corpos estranhos.

cards.front: After tissue loss, how do labile, stable and permanent tissues heal?
cards.back: **Labile** and **stable** (hepatocytes, renal tubules; re-enter the cycle from **G0**) tissues can **regenerate** if the matrix framework survives. **Permanent** cells (neurons, cardiac and skeletal myocytes) cannot divide; loss heals by **scar** (**gliosis** in the CNS). Skeletal muscle has only limited repair from **satellite cells**.
cards.back_pt: Tecidos **lábeis** e **estáveis** (hepatócitos, túbulos renais; voltam ao ciclo a partir de **G0**) podem se **regenerar** se o arcabouço da matriz for preservado. Células **permanentes** (neurônios, miócitos cardíacos e esqueléticos) não se dividem; a perda é reparada por **cicatriz (fibrose)** (**gliose** no SNC). O músculo esquelético tem reparo apenas limitado pelas **células satélites**.

cards.front: What does each main growth factor do in tissue repair?
cards.back: **VEGF**: angiogenesis. **FGF-2**: angiogenesis and fibroblast growth. **PDGF**: recruits and stimulates fibroblasts and smooth muscle cells. **TGF-β**: the main **fibrogenic** factor; increases collagen synthesis, blocks matrix breakdown and dampens inflammation.
cards.back_pt: **VEGF**: angiogênese. **FGF-2**: angiogênese e proliferação de fibroblastos. **PDGF**: recruta e estimula fibroblastos e células musculares lisas. **TGF-β**: o principal fator **fibrogênico**; aumenta a síntese de colágeno, bloqueia a degradação da matriz e atenua a inflamação.

cards.back: Local: **infection** (the most common), poor blood supply, foreign bodies, movement. Systemic: **diabetes**, **glucocorticoids** (weaker inflammation, less collagen), **vitamin C deficiency** (unstable collagen), **zinc deficiency**, malnutrition.
cards.back_pt: Locais: **infecção** (a mais comum), má irrigação, corpos estranhos, movimentação. Sistêmicos: **diabetes**, **glicocorticoides** (inflamação mais fraca, menos colágeno), **deficiência de vitamina C** (colágeno instável), **deficiência de zinco**, desnutrição.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old man has 2 days of a red, warm, swollen and painful area on his left lower leg that began around a small cut. His temperature is 39.1°C (102.4°F) and his pulse is 104/min. The leukocyte count is 15,500/mm³ with 84% neutrophils and increased band forms. He takes ibuprofen, and 1 hour later his temperature has fallen. Reduced synthesis of which mediator in the hypothalamus best explains this effect?
choices: Leukotriene B4
Histamine
Prostaglandin E2
Bradykinin
Thromboxane A2
questions.explanation: Macrophages release **IL-1**, **TNF** and **IL-6**, which induce **COX-2** in the hypothalamus. The resulting **PGE2** raises the temperature set point. NSAIDs such as ibuprofen block COX and lower fever. Ibuprofen also lowers **thromboxane A2**, but TXA2 acts on platelets and vessels and does not set body temperature. Leukotriene B4 comes from the lipoxygenase pathway, which NSAIDs do not block.
questions.explanation_pt: Os macrófagos liberam **IL-1**, **TNF** e **IL-6**, que induzem a **COX-2** no hipotálamo. A **PGE2** resultante eleva o ponto de ajuste da temperatura. AINEs como o ibuprofeno bloqueiam a COX e reduzem a febre. O ibuprofeno também reduz o **tromboxano A2**, mas o TXA2 atua em plaquetas e vasos e não regula a temperatura corporal. O leucotrieno B4 vem da via da lipoxigenase, que os AINEs não bloqueiam.

questions.stem: A 19-year-old man has 18 hours of pain that started around the umbilicus and moved to the right lower quadrant. He has nausea and a temperature of 38.3°C (100.9°F). The leukocyte count is 14,000/mm³. An appendectomy is done. Histology shows many neutrophils infiltrating the muscular wall of the appendix. Before these cells left the blood, they first slowed down and rolled along the endothelium of postcapillary venules. Which interaction mediated this rolling step?
choices: E-selectin and P-selectin on endothelium binding sialyl Lewis X on neutrophils
LFA-1 integrin (CD11a/CD18) on neutrophils binding ICAM-1 on endothelium
PECAM-1 (CD31) at the junctions between endothelial cells
C5a binding its receptor on the neutrophil surface
IgG on bacteria binding Fc receptors on neutrophils
questions.explanation: **Rolling** depends on weak, short-lived bonds between endothelial **selectins** and **sialyl Lewis X** on leukocytes. Inflammatory mediators such as TNF and IL-1 increase **E-selectin** expression, and histamine moves P-selectin stored in Weibel-Palade bodies to the cell surface. **LFA-1 binding ICAM-1** is the next step, **firm adhesion**; it is defective in leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1. PECAM-1 acts later, during transmigration.
questions.explanation_pt: O **rolamento** depende de ligações fracas e breves entre as **selectinas** endoteliais e o **sialil Lewis X** dos leucócitos. Mediadores inflamatórios como TNF e IL-1 aumentam a expressão de **E-selectina**, e a histamina leva a P-selectina armazenada nos corpúsculos de Weibel-Palade para a superfície da célula. **LFA-1 ligando-se à ICAM-1** é a etapa seguinte, a **adesão firme**; ela é defeituosa na deficiência de adesão leucocitária tipo 1. A PECAM-1 atua depois, na transmigração.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman has 2 weeks of jaundice, dark urine and fatigue after a trip abroad. Serum ALT is 1,850 U/L, and IgM antibody to hepatitis A virus is positive. She receives supportive care. Six months later she feels well, her liver tests are normal, and an ultrasound shows a normal liver. Which property of her liver best explains full recovery without scarring?
choices: Constant division of labile epithelial cells from a stem-cell pool
Replacement of lost hepatocytes by type I collagen
Hypertrophy of surviving hepatocytes without cell division
Re-entry of quiescent hepatocytes from G0 into the cell cycle on an intact reticulin framework
Differentiation of bone marrow cells into new hepatocytes
questions.explanation: Hepatocytes are **stable cells**: they normally rest in **G0** but divide again after injury. Acute hepatitis A kills hepatocytes but leaves the **reticulin (matrix) framework** intact, so new cells rebuild normal lobules. Hepatocytes are not labile cells, because they do not divide all the time. When injury is chronic and destroys the framework, healing ends in **fibrosis** (cirrhosis).
questions.explanation_pt: Os hepatócitos são **células estáveis**: normalmente ficam em **G0**, mas voltam a se dividir após lesão. A hepatite A aguda mata hepatócitos, mas preserva o **arcabouço de reticulina (matriz)**, e as novas células reconstroem lóbulos normais. Os hepatócitos não são células lábeis, pois não se dividem o tempo todo. Quando a lesão é crônica e destrói o arcabouço, a cicatrização termina em **fibrose** (cirrose).

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man lives alone and eats mostly white bread and canned meat. Three weeks ago he had abdominal surgery, and the incision has now opened again. Exam shows swollen, bleeding gums, small hemorrhages around hair follicles, corkscrew hairs on his arms, and bruises on both legs. Platelet count, PT and aPTT are normal. Which step of collagen synthesis is most likely impaired?
choices: Cross-linking of collagen fibrils by lysyl oxidase
Hydroxylation of proline and lysine residues in the rough endoplasmic reticulum
Cleavage of the terminal propeptides outside the cell
Glycosylation of hydroxylysine residues
Translation of pro-alpha chains on ribosomes
questions.explanation: This is **scurvy**. Prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases need **vitamin C**, so collagen is poorly hydroxylated and forms unstable triple helices. Weak collagen causes **poor wound healing**, gum disease and fragile vessels with **perifollicular hemorrhages**. Lysyl oxidase cross-linking needs **copper**, not vitamin C, and is defective in Menkes disease.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **escorbuto**. A prolil e a lisil hidroxilases precisam de **vitamina C**, então o colágeno fica mal hidroxilado e forma triplas hélices instáveis. O colágeno fraco causa **má cicatrização**, doença gengival e vasos frágeis com **hemorragias perifoliculares**. A ligação cruzada pela lisil oxidase depende de **cobre**, e não de vitamina C, e está alterada na doença de Menkes.

notes.title: Inflammation and repair: acute, chronic, systemic effects and healing
notes.body_md:
## Acute inflammation

- Triggers: microbes, necrotic tissue, foreign bodies and immune reactions.
- **Vascular phase**: arteriolar dilation (redness, heat) and leaky **postcapillary venules** (swelling). The fluid is an **exudate**, rich in protein and cells.
- **Cellular phase**: **neutrophils** dominate the first day; **macrophages** replace them within 1-2 days.
- Neutrophil recruitment: rolling (**selectins**), firm adhesion (**integrins** binding **ICAM-1**), transmigration and **chemotaxis** (C5a, LTB4, IL-8).
- Mediators: **histamine** (fast leak), **prostaglandins** (vasodilation, pain, fever), **leukotrienes** (leak, bronchospasm; LTB4 attracts neutrophils), **bradykinin** (leak, pain), **C3a and C5a** (trigger mast cell degranulation; C5a attracts neutrophils).
- NSAIDs block COX and prostaglandin synthesis: see the musculoskeletal pharmacology block.

## Outcomes

- **Resolution**: brief injury with little tissue loss.
- **Abscess**: pus walled off by granulation tissue, then fibrous tissue; often needs drainage.
- **Fistula**: an abnormal tract between two epithelial surfaces (e.g., Crohn disease).
- **Fibrosis**: large tissue loss, or a fibrin-rich exudate that is not cleared.
- **Chronic inflammation**: the cause persists.

## Chronic and granulomatous inflammation

- **Macrophages**, **lymphocytes** and **plasma cells**; injury and repair happen together.
- In granulomas, **Th1** cells release **IFN-γ**, which turns macrophages into **epithelioid cells** and giant cells.

## Systemic effects

- **IL-1**, **TNF** and **IL-6** cause **fever** through hypothalamic **PGE2**.
- Bacterial infection: **leukocytosis** with band forms (**left shift**).
- The liver makes **acute-phase proteins** (CRP, fibrinogen, hepcidin): see the immunology block.

## Repair

- **Regeneration** needs cells that can divide and an intact matrix framework; otherwise the tissue heals by **scar**.
- **Granulation tissue**: new capillaries, fibroblasts and type III collagen, later replaced by type I. Wound healing phases and keloids: see the skin block.
- Organ fibrosis: **cirrhosis**, pulmonary fibrosis, scar after myocardial infarction.
- Poor healing: infection, ischemia, diabetes, glucocorticoids, vitamin C or zinc deficiency.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Inflamação aguda

- Gatilhos: micróbios, tecido necrótico, corpos estranhos e reações imunes.
- **Fase vascular**: dilatação arteriolar (rubor, calor) e **vênulas pós-capilares** permeáveis (edema). O líquido é um **exsudato**, rico em proteínas e células.
- **Fase celular**: os **neutrófilos** predominam no primeiro dia; os **macrófagos** os substituem em 1-2 dias.
- Recrutamento de neutrófilos: rolamento (**selectinas**), adesão firme (**integrinas** ligando-se à **ICAM-1**), transmigração e **quimiotaxia** (C5a, LTB4, IL-8).
- Mediadores: **histamina** (extravasamento rápido), **prostaglandinas** (vasodilatação, dor, febre), **leucotrienos** (extravasamento, broncoespasmo; o LTB4 atrai neutrófilos), **bradicinina** (extravasamento, dor), **C3a e C5a** (degranulação de mastócitos; o C5a atrai neutrófilos).
- Os AINEs bloqueiam a COX e a síntese de prostaglandinas: veja o bloco de farmacologia musculoesquelética.

## Desfechos

- **Resolução**: lesão breve com pouca perda de tecido.
- **Abscesso**: pus delimitado por tecido de granulação e depois por tecido fibroso; muitas vezes precisa de drenagem.
- **Fístula**: trajeto anormal entre duas superfícies epiteliais (ex.: doença de Crohn).
- **Fibrose**: grande perda de tecido, ou exsudato rico em fibrina que não é removido.
- **Inflamação crônica**: a causa persiste.

## Inflamação crônica e granulomatosa

- **Macrófagos**, **linfócitos** e **plasmócitos**; lesão e reparo acontecem juntos.
- Nos granulomas, células **Th1** liberam **IFN-γ**, que transforma macrófagos em **células epitelioides** e células gigantes.

## Efeitos sistêmicos

- **IL-1**, **TNF** e **IL-6** causam **febre** por meio da **PGE2** hipotalâmica.
- Infecção bacteriana: **leucocitose** com bastonetes (**desvio à esquerda**).
- O fígado produz **proteínas de fase aguda** (PCR, fibrinogênio, hepcidina): veja o bloco de imunologia.

## Reparo

- A **regeneração** exige células capazes de se dividir e um arcabouço de matriz íntegro; caso contrário, o tecido cicatriza com **fibrose (cicatriz)**.
- **Tecido de granulação**: novos capilares, fibroblastos e colágeno tipo III, depois substituído pelo tipo I. Fases da cicatrização de feridas e queloides: veja o bloco de pele.
- Fibrose em órgãos: **cirrose**, fibrose pulmonar, cicatriz após infarto do miocárdio.
- Má cicatrização: infecção, isquemia, diabetes, glicocorticoides, deficiência de vitamina C ou de zinco.
